A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hilbert-space PCA framework, with matching authors, datasets, and appendices A–G. Their text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Gaussian simulations and analyses of HIPC and ModelNet10. Appendix G contains further Gaussian and Sentinel-2 image experiments.

after.justification: Original simulation and real-data results remain, and Tables 2–3 add empirical studies of ambient dimension and the number of PCA components.

M1.justification: The KME, LOT, and SW embeddings, empirical covariance estimator, and PCA procedure are unchanged. Barycentric projection was already used in v1, Equation (10); its added theoretical treatment does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Table 2 extends Gaussian evaluation from the original d = 2 setting to higher-dimensional inputs with d = 5, 10, and 50. HIPC, ModelNet10, and the Gaussian and Sentinel-2 experiments in Appendix G remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same three evaluated alternatives: KME, LOT, and SW. The new dimension and component-count tables also use this set; no additional cited method becomes an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes dense-regime discretization (m0, T, p) from (500, 20, 20) to (100, 10, 10), and sparse-regime discretization from (100, 10, 10) to (500, 40, 40). Figure 2 now plots m = 100–500, although v2's text still states 10–500. The principal metrics and real-data evaluation procedure remain.

E4.justification: New Tables 2–3 substantially expand sensitivity analysis by testing two previously unexamined dependencies: covariance and excess risks versus ambient dimension, and excess risk versus retained component count q = 1, 2, 5, 10. Existing subsampling-stability analyses, including Appendix G, are retained.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 explicitly reduces simulation averaging from 20 independent trials to 10. Real-data experiments retain 20 subsamples and mean/standard-deviation reporting. The new tables include ± quantities, but their statistical meaning is not explicitly identified.

E6.justification: Figures 1–2 contain revised simulation results under changed settings. Whereas v1 describes dense-regime excess risk as decaying like n^(-1/2), v2 reports slopes of -0.919, -0.908, and -0.925 for KME, LOT, and SW. Tables 2–3 add dimension- and component-dependent results; for example, Table 3 reports LOT excess risk increasing from 4.13 to 39.09 as q increases from 1 to 10, with values multiplied by 100. Real-data and Appendix G figures are unchanged.

T1.justification: The bounded-embedding premise of v1's Theorem 3.7 is replaced by fourth-moment and explicit subgaussian assumptions in v2's Theorem 3.8, with revised dependence on R. Appendix C.3 replaces the Lipschitz/Wasserstein argument with a Hilbert–Schmidt bound. V2 also adds unequal-sample-size and operator-norm extensions, a claimed projection-error corollary with proof, and Theorem F.7 on barycentric-projection estimation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: double-asymptotic covariance and excess-risk rates, a sparse-to-dense transition, dense-regime minimax optimality for covariance estimation, and accurate PCA through subsampling.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation linking eigenvalue decay to kernel smoothness and discusses why ordinary FPCA components can leave probability space. It also interprets Table 2 as showing LOT deterioration while KME and SW remain essentially stable, although KME covariance risk also rises from 1.43 to 12.64 in the table's displayed units.

D1.justification: Documented reference-point, projection, and quantile counts are revised, and Section 4.2 adds a formula for the existing Procrustes calculation. Neither version supplies code or hardware information. The new sweeps specify which variables are held fixed without fully reporting their fixed values.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bosq (2000), Ramsay and Silverman (2005), and Davis and Kahan (1969), supporting eigenvalue-decay discussion and the projection-error connection. It also expands discussion of FPCA's limitations and the already-cited barycentric-projection literature; the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: There are focused introductory explanations, additional remarks, author-year citations, publication-header edits, and some Appendix C reorganization. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain, including the abstract and conclusion.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout. Figures 1–2 are redrawn with logarithmic axes, fitted slopes, markers, and dashed lines; Tables 2–3 are added. Figures 3–6 move from pages interspersed with references into the main discussion and are substantially resized. Appendix G figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: Explicit subgaussian assumptions and the new sensitivity studies and convergence slopes improve transparency and empirical support. However, new Corollary 3.9 and Appendix C.4 divide by λ(q+1) − λ(q) despite assuming decreasing eigenvalues, making the projection-error bound invalid as written. Incompletely specified controls also limit reproducibility of the new tables. These substantive gains and correctness concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
